title: Take a baby's temperature under its arm with a digital stick thermometer
instruction: Take the infant care manikin's temperature under its right arm with the digital stick thermometer, leave the reading on show with the thermometer display up on the mat, put the arm back at its side and switch the thermometer off.
context: Taking a child's temperature under the arm is something most parents and carers have done. The thermometer's manual: turn it on with the On/Off button, "place the probe tip under the arm so the tip is touching the skin", wait for the peak (usually 11 s underarm), signalled by 5 beeps, read it, then turn it off with the button (it turns itself off after about 1.5 min). The hard part is physical: the 4 mm tip has to stay on the skin under the closed arm for the whole count, and any break restarts it. A baby's arm falls back when it is let go, and so does this manikin's: below about 70 deg its shoulder joint does not hold the arm up. So one hand lifts the arm and holds it up while the other slides the light stick (est 15 g) in along the mat until the tip touches the armpit; then the arm is lowered onto the stick and holds it there. Lowered carelessly, the arm pushes the stick out of place and the count never finishes.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top (z 0); arm bases at y +305 and -305. Nothing is clamped. (1) Changing mat, loose: a flat wipe-clean changing pad, mid-blue PVC over foam, 460 x 600 x 15 mm (est size), from x 60 to 520 and y -300 to +300; top at z 15. (2) Infant care manikin, loose, on its back on the mat: a newborn-size baby care manikin as used in parenting classes (Nasco SB17159 class, listed 21 in or 53 cm, 5 lb or 2.3 kg; soft vinyl, medium brown skin tone, jointed arms and legs, white diaper on), newborn proportions: a head 120 mm across (about a quarter of its length), short limbs, no painted face (simulated with simple rounded and box shapes). It lies along y, crown at y +284, soles at y -238, midline on x 300, head to the robot's left, so its right arm is on the robot's side. Torso est 124 mm wide (x 238 to 362) and 85 mm deep. Right arm: one moulded piece with the elbow slightly bent, est 175 mm from shoulder to fingertips, 0.10 kg, 35 mm thick at the upper arm, 30 at the forearm, 26 at the hand, on the manikin's shoulder disc joint, which turns about its left-right axis (along x) at y 135, z 35.5: the joint swings the arm forward and up, so the armpit is opened by raising the arm. At rest it lies along the body toward the feet (y +140 to -37, x 199 to 234 at the upper arm), its inner face 3.5 mm from the armpit sensor film and its underside 3 mm above the mat. Joint friction est 0.02 N m; the arm's weight gives about 0.07 N m about the joint when it is flat, so let go below about 70 deg it sinks back onto the manikin's side or onto whatever is under it (measure both on the real manikin). Armpit sensor: a thin-film force sensor, Interlink FSR 402 (listed: 14.68 mm active disc, 0.46 mm thick, 0.2 to 20 N), taped flat on the torso side under the upper arm, its disc facing the robot at x 238, centred at y 90 (45 mm toward the feet from the shoulder axis), z 25; its tail runs down the torso side to the mat and on to a logger read every 50 ms. In simulation the film is part of the manikin. The head, the other limbs and the diaper are fixed in pose. (3) Thermometer, loose, switched off, display up: Vicks SpeedRead V912US digital stick thermometer, white plastic, about 114 mm long and 13 mm thick (listed), body est 22 mm wide, tapering over its front 30 mm to a 4 mm metal tip, est 15 g; one round grey-blue On/Off button est 10 mm across, 28 mm from the tail end, est 2 N over 0.8 mm of travel; a display window est 22 x 10 mm, 36 to 58 mm from the tail: dark and blank when off, lit green when on. It lies along x at y -140 beside the manikin's right hand, tail at x 100, tip at x 214 pointing away from the robot. Friction, est (incline test in the README): manikin vinyl on mat 0.5, thermometer on mat 0.4. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every 50 ms step: poses, the manikin's shoulder angle (0 deg = arm flat), the button's travel, the thermometer's state and the grippers. Switching, as on the unit: a press of 0.3 mm or more released within 5 s turns it on or off (a 5 s hold opens the C/F setting instead); ready 2 s after switching on; it turns itself off 90 s after switching on if no reading is taken, and 90 s after a reading. Closed (contact, not nearness): on and ready, the metal tip (its front 8 mm) within 0.5 mm of the armpit sensor disc (touching: resting surfaces read 0 to 0.25 mm), the thermometer within 0.5 mm of the manikin's right arm (the arm resting on it), the shoulder at 22 deg or less (the arm rests about 13 to 15 deg up on the stick). Real: the sensor, calibrated with a 20 g weight, reads 0.2 N or more; the side video shows the hand's centre 76 mm or less over the mat; the top video shows the upper arm on the stick. Reading: Closed on every step for 11.0 s unbroken; a break restarts the count; then the display holds the result until the unit is off (real: the sensor log shows 0.2 N or more for 11.0 s unbroken while the video shows the arm down, then the display shows Lo, the unit's completed reading below 32.0 C as on a room-temperature manikin, or a temperature; Err does not count). Shown: after the reading, while on, the thermometer lies on the mat (lowest point within 4 mm of the mat top), out of the armpit (tip 30 mm or more from the disc, no part within 10 mm of the manikin's arm), display facing within 30 deg of straight up, every finger of both grippers 30 mm or more from it, for 2.0 s unbroken. Arm back: shoulder at 5 deg or less (real: the hand's centre 30 mm or less over the mat). Off: turned off with its button after Shown, and off now. Score 0 for the run only for unsafe handling: the manikin taken off the mat (its back's midline point outside the mat top), lifted (that point more than 30 mm over the mat top) or rolled over (more than 45 deg from lying on its back); or any part of the thermometer 5 mm or more below the mat top (fell off the mat). Shifting or turning the manikin on the mat is not penalised (the sensor moves with it). Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 Reading, Shown, Arm back and Off, with every finger of both grippers 30 mm or more from manikin and thermometer on every step of the last 1 s and the thermometer, the manikin and its hand each moved 5 mm or less over that 1 s; 0.75 Reading, Shown and Arm back (not all of the rest: left on, off by itself, or still touched); 0.5 a Reading (not shown for 2 s, arm not back, or switched off before Shown); 0.25 Closed at some step but no Reading; 0 otherwise. Doing nothing scores 0. Success: 1.0 held 1 s. Real trial: the mat's edge, a 30 mm block by the manikin's back and the side video for the unsafe-handling checks; a side video with an upright ruler by the manikin's hand for the arm checks; the sensor log, synced to the video, times Closed; the video shows each press, the display lighting or going blank, and the display face up for 2 s; a 30 mm block for hands off.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The manikin is one rigid body; its right arm is one rigid piece on a revolute (the shoulder disc joint, friction est 0.02 N m). Vinyl skin does not give. The button is a sprung slider. The reading is a declared rule following the manual: on, tip on the armpit under the lowered arm, 11.0 s unbroken. No temperature is simulated; the display is a drawn face the rule slides under the window (blank off, lit with Lo on).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the manikin on its back inside its tape outline on the mat, both arms at its sides. Away from the rig, wipe the thermometer tip with an alcohol wipe and let it dry. Check the armpit sensor is flat, taped down and reads zero with the arm at the side. Check the thermometer is off (display blank), then lay it display up on its tape mark beside the manikin's right hand, tip pointing away from the robot. Replace its CR1225 cell when the display dims. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (one arm idle: 0.0 left idle, 0.0 right idle)
